summary: Liechtenstein applies Schengen rules through its association agreement: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, nationals of the 64 countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (as of 30 December 2025) get 90 days in any 180-day period, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa, applied for in most places at the Swiss representation where they live.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Liechtenstein?
faq.answer: Liechtenstein follows Schengen rules: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, and nationals of the 64 countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (as of 30 December 2025) (among them the US, UK, Canada and Japan) can stay 90 days in any 180-day period. Everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa.

faq.question: Does Liechtenstein issue its own visas?
faq.answer: Applications go through Swiss missions in most places: Liechtenstein's Immigration and Passport Office says visa-required people apply at the Swiss representation where they live, and that the decision lies partly with the Swiss authorities and partly with the Office. In some cities, including New Delhi, Kuala Lumpur, Dublin and Minsk, Austria, Hungary or Lithuania takes the application instead.

faq.question: Does time in Liechtenstein count toward my 90 Schengen days?
faq.answer: Yes. Liechtenstein is part of the Schengen Area, so days spent there count toward the same 90-days-in-180 limit as the rest of the area.

faq.question: What currency does Liechtenstein use?
faq.answer: The Swiss franc (CHF), according to Canada's travel advice.
